# CLI

## `roomba-kit`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Roomba Kit: local-first control for iRobot robots.

  Most commands talk to the background service (`roomba-kit service start`). Lifecycle
  and token commands work without it.

Options:
  --json             Machine output: the HTTP JSON body.
  --service-url URL  The service to talk to. Default: http://127.0.0.1:<server.port>
                     from config.toml (http://127.0.0.1:8765). Env:
                     ROOMBA_KIT_SERVICE_URL.
  -q, --quiet        Suppress non-essential output.
  -h, --help         Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  capabilities  What the robot's model supports, each with `verified` (exercised on...
  clean         Start cleaning the whole home.
  cloud         The optional iRobot account: login, status, passwords.
  config        Where the kit keeps its files, and what's in them.
  coverage      Where a finished mission cleaned: covered points, dirt detections...
  discover      Find iRobot robots on the local network: ID, name, SKU, firmware,...
  dock          Send the robot back to its dock.
  evac          Empty the bin into the Clean Base.
  events
  find          Play the locate sound so you can find the robot.
  floor-plan    The robot's stored map from the iRobot cloud: its rooms with names,...
  health        Whether the service is up, and its version.
  missions
  pause         Pause the current mission.
  position      Where the robot is now: x/y in metres from the dock and heading in...
  reboot        Soft-reboot the robot.
  resume        Resume a paused mission.
  robots        Add, list, pair and remove robots.
  serve         Run the service in the foreground on `server.host`:`server.port`.
  service       Run the service in the background and manage it.
  settings      Read and change robot settings (read back).
  setup         Guided setup: find robots, pair them, and optionally add an iRobot...
  state         Get a robot's full live state: battery, activity, current mission,...
  stop          End the current mission where the robot is.
  token         Create, list and revoke API tokens (local file ops).
  train         Start a mapping run with no cleaning.
  verify        Check capabilities against the real robot and record the run:...
  version       Print the kit version.
```

## `roomba-kit cloud history`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit cloud history [OPTIONS] ROBOT

  The robot's recent missions as the iRobot cloud recorded them (it keeps about 30),
  newest first. A running mission appears only minutes after the robot docks. While the
  cloud is unavailable, the last copy fetched is returned.

  Parameters:
  - `robot`: str — Robot ID or name
  - `limit`: int (default: 30) — Most recent missions to return

  Supported on: braava_m6, roomba_i5

  Verification: braava_m6: verified, roomba_i5: verified

Options:
  --limit INTEGER  Most recent missions to return  [default: (30)]
  -h, --help       Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit cloud login`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit cloud login [OPTIONS]

  Add or change the iRobot account login. It's checked by logging in and saved only if
  that works. Optional: it adds room names, floor plans, cloud history, coverage, the
  live mission timeline and password retrieval; local control never needs it.

  Parameters:
  - `username`: str — iRobot account email
  - `password`: str — iRobot account password. The CLI prompts for it; it is never echoed, returned or logged.
  - `country`: str (default: 'US') — The account's country code, e.g. US, GB, DE

Options:
  --username TEXT  iRobot account email  [required]
  --country TEXT   The account's country code, e.g. US, GB, DE  [default: (US)]
  -h, --help       Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit cloud logout`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit cloud logout [OPTIONS]

  Remove the stored iRobot account login and disconnect from the cloud. Credentials
  supplied by environment variables still apply.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
```

```text
Usage: roomba-kit cloud password [OPTIONS] ROBOT

  Parameters:
  - `robot`: str — Robot ID or unambiguous name
```

```text
Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit coverage`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit coverage [OPTIONS] ROBOT MISSION_ID

  Where a finished mission cleaned: covered points, dirt detections and clutter, in
  metres from the dock. The cloud publishes it minutes after the robot docks; until then
  this returns `cloud_unavailable` with reason `not_yet_published`. Clutter is given as
  the vertices of each clutter area's outline.

  Parameters:
  - `robot`: str — Robot ID or name
  - `mission_id`: str — The kit mission ID (the robot's own mission ID) or the cloud mission ref

  Supported on: braava_m6, roomba_i5

  Verification: braava_m6: verified, roomba_i5: verified

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit discover`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit discover [OPTIONS]

  Find iRobot robots on the local network: ID, name, SKU, firmware, address, whether the
  model is supported, and whether it's already configured.

  Parameters:
  - `broadcast`: str | None (default: None) — Where to send the discovery datagram: your subnet's broadcast address (e.g. 192.0.2.255) when a VPN owns the default route, or one robot's IP. Default: `[discovery] broadcast` in config.toml
  - `timeout_s`: float (default: 8.0) — How long to listen

Options:
  --broadcast TEXT   Where to send the discovery datagram: your subnet's broadcast
                     address (e.g. 192.0.2.255) when a VPN owns the default route, or
                     one robot's IP. Default: `[discovery] broadcast` in config.toml
  --timeout-s FLOAT  How long to listen  [default: (8.0)]
  -h, --help         Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit events list`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit events list [OPTIONS]

  List recorded events, oldest first, after `since`. Over HTTP, send `Accept:
  text/event-stream` to get the same events as a live SSE stream that resumes with
  `Last-Event-ID`.

  Parameters:
  - `since`: int | None (default: None) — Return events with a seq greater than this; omit for the oldest
  - `robot`: str | None (default: None) — Only this robot (ID or unambiguous name)
  - `types`: list[roomba_kit.core.events.EventType] | None (default: None) — Only these event types
  - `limit`: int (default: 100) — Most events to return

Options:
  --since INTEGER                 Return events with a seq greater than this; omit for
                                  the oldest
  --robot TEXT                    Only this robot (ID or unambiguous name)
  --types [state.changed|activity.changed|mission.started|mission.finished|robot.docked|robot.stuck|bin.full|error.raised|error.cleared|connection.changed|setting.changed|cloud.status|cloud.timeline|position|alert.dock_search_timeout]
                                  Only these event types
  --limit INTEGER                 Most events to return  [default: (100)]
  -h, --help                      Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit events wait`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit events wait [OPTIONS]

  Wait for events after `since` and return them as soon as any arrive, or an empty list
  at the timeout. Call again with `next` to keep following.

  Parameters:
  - `since`: int — Wait for events with a seq greater than this
  - `robot`: str | None (default: None) — Only this robot (ID or unambiguous name)
  - `types`: list[roomba_kit.core.events.EventType] | None (default: None) — Only these event types
  - `timeout_s`: float (default: 30) — Seconds to wait before returning no events

Options:
  --since INTEGER                 Wait for events with a seq greater than this
                                  [required]
  --robot TEXT                    Only this robot (ID or unambiguous name)
  --types [state.changed|activity.changed|mission.started|mission.finished|robot.docked|robot.stuck|bin.full|error.raised|error.cleared|connection.changed|setting.changed|cloud.status|cloud.timeline|position|alert.dock_search_timeout]
                                  Only these event types
  --timeout-s FLOAT               Seconds to wait before returning no events  [default:
                                  (30)]
  -h, --help                      Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit events watch`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit events watch [OPTIONS]

  Follow events live, one line each (`--json`: one envelope per line). Ctrl-C to stop.

Options:
  --robot TEXT                    Only this robot (ID or unambiguous name)
  --type [state.changed|activity.changed|mission.started|mission.finished|robot.docked|robot.stuck|bin.full|error.raised|error.cleared|connection.changed|setting.changed|cloud.status|cloud.timeline|position|alert.dock_search_timeout]

  --since INTEGER                 Replay events after this seq first
```


## `roomba-kit missions wait`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit missions wait [OPTIONS] ROBOT

  Wait until a robot's mission ends and return it with its outcome. Without `mission_id`
  it waits for the current mission, or the next one if none is running. Returns
  `{timeout: true, mission}` if it hasn't ended in time.

  Parameters:
  - `robot`: str — Robot ID or unambiguous name
  - `mission_id`: str | None (default: None) — The mission to wait for; omit for the current or next mission
  - `timeout_s`: float (default: 1800) — Seconds to wait for the mission to end

Options:
  --mission-id TEXT  The mission to wait for; omit for the current or next mission
  --timeout-s FLOAT  Seconds to wait for the mission to end  [default: (1800)]
  -h, --help         Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit position`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit position [OPTIONS] ROBOT

  Where the robot is now: x/y in metres from the dock and heading in radians, with the
  map it's on. `{no_fix: true}` when it has no fix (for example while docked); that is
  not an error. During missions the same fixes stream as `position` events.

  Parameters:
  - `robot`: str — Robot ID or name

  Supported on: braava_m6

  Verification: braava_m6: verified

  With --watch, print the current answer, then every fix as it arrives (Ctrl-C to stop).
  Fixes arrive while the robot is cleaning or returning.

Options:
  --watch     Follow live position fixes.
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit robots add`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit robots add [OPTIONS] ADDRESS

  Add the robot at an IP address, for when discovery can't reach it. The robot must
  answer there. Next, give it a password with `retrieve_password`.

  Parameters:
  - `address`: str — The robot's IP address

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit robots list`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit robots list [OPTIONS]

  List every configured robot: ID, name, model, SKU, firmware, address, connection state
  and capabilities with their verification status. Robots without a model profile are

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit robots password`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit robots password [OPTIONS] ROBOT

  Pair a robot: retrieve its password while you hold HOME, or --manual to type it.

  Either way it's verified by connecting before it's stored, and never shown.

Options:
  --manual           Type the password instead of retrieving it.
  --timeout-s FLOAT  How long to keep retrying (default 60).
  -h, --help         Show this message and exit.
```

```text
Usage: roomba-kit robots remove [OPTIONS] ROBOT

  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit service install`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit service install [OPTIONS]

  Start the service automatically: a launchd agent on macOS, a systemd user unit on
  Linux.

  It runs `serve` with this Python and pins the current config and state dirs. Logs go
  to `<state>/service.log`. Exits 69 if it's installed but not healthy within the
  timeout.

Options:
  --print          Print the unit; install nothing.
  --timeout FLOAT  Seconds to wait for health.  [default: 10.0]
  -h, --help       Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit service logs`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit service logs [OPTIONS]

  Show the background service's log.

Options:
  -n, --lines INTEGER  Lines of history to show.  [default: 50]
  -f, --follow         Keep printing new lines.
  -h, --help           Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit service start`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit service start [OPTIONS]

  Start the service in the background.

  Waits until `/v1/health` answers. Logs go to `<state>/service.log`.

Options:
```


## `roomba-kit settings set`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit settings set [OPTIONS] ROBOT SETTING VALUE

  Change one setting. It is reported applied only once the robot reports the new value;
  otherwise the error is `not_applied` with the value the robot holds.

  Parameters:
  - `robot`: str — Robot ID or name
  - `setting`: str — Setting name: passes, edge_clean, always_finish, child_lock, eco_charge, schedule_hold, pad_wetness or spray_overlap
  - `value`: bool | int | str — passes: auto|one|two. edge_clean, always_finish, child_lock, eco_charge, schedule_hold: true|false. pad_wetness: 1|2|3. spray_overlap: standard|deep|extended.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
```

```text
Options:
```

## `roomba-kit state`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit state [OPTIONS] ROBOT

  Get a robot's full live state: battery, activity, current mission, last command, error

```

```text
  List API tokens: name, created and last used. Token values are never shown.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit token revoke`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit token revoke [OPTIONS] NAME

  Revoke an API token. The service rejects it from its next request.

  Parameters:
  - `name`: str — Token name, e.g. `cli` or `home-assistant`

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit train`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit train [OPTIONS] ROBOT

  Start a mapping run with no cleaning. Confirmed when the robot reports mapping. ⚠ This
  can re-create the stored map and change room IDs, which breaks room names and room-
  clean requests that use the old IDs.

  Parameters:
  - `robot`: str — Robot ID or unambiguous name

  Supported on: braava_m6, roomba_i5

  Verification: braava_m6: unverified, roomba_i5: unverified

  ⚠ Moves the robot: it will physically start, stop or drive.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
```

## `roomba-kit verify`

```text
Usage: roomba-kit verify [OPTIONS] ROBOT [CAPABILITIES]...

  Check capabilities against the real robot and record the run: settings are written,
  read back and restored; commands are issued and confirmed (only `find` without
  allow_motion). Returns each result with evidence, plus a markdown report for
  `docs/verification/<profile>.md`.

  Parameters:
  - `robot`: str — Robot ID or name
  - `capabilities`: list[str] | None (default: None) — Capabilities to check, e.g. `setting.passes find`. Default: every one the model declares (`train` is only ever run when named here)
  - `allow_motion`: bool (default: False) — Run checks that act on the robot (every command except `find`). Without it they are skipped

  ⚠ Moves the robot: it will physically start, stop or drive.

  With --allow-motion the command asks before moving the robot (skip with --yes).

Options:
  --allow-motion / --no-allow-motion
                                  Run checks that act on the robot (every command except
                                  `find`). Without it they are skipped  [default:
                                  (False)]
  --write-report                  Append the report to docs/verification/<profile>.md
                                  (run from the repo).
  -y, --yes                       Don't prompt before motion checks.
  -h, --help                      Show this message and exit.
```
